lines: Taylor Nguyen
+1 (555) 010-6642 | taylor.nguyen@example.com | example.com/code/tnguyen
EDUCATION
Westfield State University | M.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Westfield State University | B.S. in Computer Science | Metro City, USA | Sep 2019 - Jun 2023
EXPERIENCE
Westfield State University | Web Developer, IT Services | Metro City, USA | Jul 2023 - Aug 2024
- Owned the department websites and the shared component library other developers relied on.
- Interviewed 8 department editors about publishing; the findings led to a preview mode that cut broken pages reported by students from 30 to 6 a month.
- Wrote the accessibility checklist for all university web pages, reducing failed audits from 12 to 2 a semester.
- Rebuilt the course-catalog search with client-side filtering, cutting search time from 4 seconds to under 1.
Lumen Travel | Frontend Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Sep 2025
- Improved page performance by 35% by code-splitting the calendar and map widgets.
- Added keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels to the date picker, fixing all 14 accessibility issues flagged in the audit.
- Wrote 60 component tests for the search filters, which caught 3 regressions before release.
- Cut the landing page's largest contentful paint from 4.1s to 1.2s by adding loading="lazy" to the hero image.
- Prevented cross-site scripting in comments by storing user input in React state before rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
- Rebuilt the hotel search results page in React with server-side rendering, cutting median load time from 3.8s to 1.6s and raising bookings per search 9% in an A/B test.
PROJECTS
Transit Arrival Web App | Independent Project | TypeScript, React | Oct 2025 - Present
- Built a progressive web app showing live bus arrivals for 400 stops, used by about 900 riders a week.
- Cached the stop list offline, so the app opened in 0.8s on a slow 3G connection against 2.9s before.
- Open-sourced the app, and the city transit agency linked it from its developer page.
Library Room Booking | Hackathon, Team of 4 | Vue | Feb 2024 - Mar 2024
- Worked on the frontend of the booking flow using React and TypeScript.
- Wrote the booking calendar component and its tests, handling overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
- Rebuilt a travel search page with server rendering, more than halving its load time and lifting bookings by about a tenth.
SKILLS
Tools: TypeScript, React, Vue, Storybok, Angular
Methods: server-side rendering, accessibility, component testing

items.says: Check that the code link leads directly to work you want an employer to see.
items.because: The link should support your candidacy.

items.says: For experienced-hire roles, consider putting experience before education.
items.because: The most relevant evidence would appear sooner.

items.says: Put the 2025 Lumen role above the 2023–24 university role.
items.because: Reverse chronological order makes the timeline easier to scan.

items.says: Specify the scope of ownership, such as the number of sites or maintenance responsibilities.
items.because: “Owned” and “other developers relied on” are broad claims without that context.

items.says: Clarify how and over what period the broken-page counts were measured.
items.because: That makes the connection between preview mode and the result credible.

items.says: Narrow or substantiate “all university web pages.”
items.because: The stated scope needs to be precise.

items.says: Explain what “failed audits” counts.
items.because: The stated result needs to be precise.

items.says: Identify what “search time” measures.
items.because: It helps readers interpret the performance claim.

items.says: Clarify whether client-side filtering remained workable for the catalog’s size.
items.because: It helps readers interpret the performance claim.

items.says: Name the metric behind the 35% performance improvement.
items.because: “Page performance” alone is too vague to evaluate.

items.says: Give the measurement conditions for the 35% improvement.
items.because: “Page performance” alone is too vague to evaluate.

items.says: Ensure “all 14” refers to issues your changes actually resolved.
items.because: That distinction matters in accessibility claims.

items.says: Indicate the testing tool or the behavior the component tests covered, if space permits.
items.because: A little context makes the work more concrete.

items.says: The hero-image LCP bullet needs its implementation and causal attribution corrected or substantiated.
items.because: Lazy-loading a hero image can worsen largest contentful paint if that image is the LCP element.

items.says: Storing input in React state does not prevent XSS when rendering it with dangerouslySetInnerHTML.
items.because: The bullet describes a potential vulnerability as a security fix.

items.says: Check that the A/B result is attributable to your work.
Be ready to explain the A/B result’s measurement and your contribution.
Say how the roughly 900 weekly riders were measured and keep the figure current.
items.because: Real usage is valuable when it is verifiable.

items.says: Clarify whether 0.8s measures an offline open or a slow-3G open.
items.because: Those describe different conditions.

items.says: The React and TypeScript frontend bullet conflicts with the project heading’s Vue stack.
items.because: Both should accurately describe the project.

items.says: Verify that the tests cover both overlapping bookings and time-zone changes.
The travel-search bullet is misplaced in the library project and closely duplicates the Lumen hotel-search result.
items.because: Travel bookings appear unrelated to library room booking.

items.says: “Storybok” is misspelled.
Keep Angular only if you can discuss or demonstrate working proficiency.
items.because: An unsupported skill can become an interview problem.

items.says: Make sure each listed method is supported by the experience or projects above.
items.because: The section should reinforce the evidence, not make new claims.
